transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um... I guess I'm here because... well, I've been having some trouble. Once I start eating, it's like... I don't know. It feels like I just disappear, and something else takes over. Even while I'm in my head telling myself to stop, I just... I keep going. Until I can't stand it anymore. So... yeah. That's it, really.
Can you tell me more about that feeling of not being able to stop eating, even when you want to? Does it happen suddenly, or does it build up over time?

I don't know... it's hard to explain. I guess it just kind of... happens. Like I don't really see it coming until I'm already doing it. I don't really think about it building up or anything. It's just... I'm eating, and then I can't stop.
When you're eating and you feel like you can't stop, does it feel like you're losing control of yourself or what's happening?

Yeah... I mean, I guess I already said that. It's just like I disappear. Something else is in charge. I'm there in my head, telling myself to stop, but... I just keep going. Until I physically can't anymore. So, yeah. I guess that's losing control.
Do these episodes bother you or affect your daily life in any way?

Um... yeah, I guess. I mean... I've kind of stopped going to meals with people from my dorm. Or hanging out with them much. I just... I don't want them to notice how I am around food. And... school is kind of a mess right now. It's hard to study when... I don't know. When whole nights just get taken over by... planning it, or just trying to recover from it afterward. So... yeah. It affects things.
After these episodes of eating, do you feel guilty, ashamed, or upset with yourself?
Yeah... I mean, I guess so. It's... not a great feeling. I just try not to think about it too much after it's done.
After these episodes of eating, do you ever make yourself sick or do anything extreme to try to compensate for what you've eaten?

Um... yeah. I guess I do. It's just... I get really scared about it. About all that food just sitting there, turning into weight. So... I'll usually find a bathroom somewhere. Like, in the dorm, or maybe up on one of the quiet floors in the library. And... yeah. I make myself throw up.
Do you find yourself eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most people would eat in a similar period under similar circumstances?

Um... yeah. I guess. Like... sometimes after studying, I'll go from the dining hall back to my room and... just eat. A lot. 

Burgers, cereal... peanut butter, whatever snacks I can get. It's... definitely way more than a normal dinner. I just... I don't stop until the trash is full and I feel sick. So... yeah.
Can you tell me if you feel like you're not in control during these episodes of eating a lot?

Yeah... I guess so. It's... it's kind of why I came in. Once I start, it just feels like... like I disappear, you know? Like something else takes over. Even when I'm sitting there, in my head, telling myself to just stop... I can't. I just keep going until I physically can't stand it anymore.
Do you usually eat this large amount of food in secret, like when you're alone or when you don't want others to see?
Um... yeah. Usually. I don't really... like people being around. So, yeah, I'm by myself.
How often do these episodes happen? Like, how many times a week or month would you say you feel this way and end up eating like that?

Um... I don't know exactly. A lot. It's been going on for most of this semester, really. Like... several times a week. It's not just a once-in-a-while thing. For the last few months, at least, there hasn't really been a week where it stopped. Just... eating, and then throwing up. Over and over.
Do you often feel unable to stop eating or feel that you're not in control during these episodes even when you're not followed by making yourself sick?
Um... no. Not really. If I start eating like that... I always end up getting sick after. So... I don't think so.
